newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng scores record close, but off highs.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng scores record close, but off highs.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng index scored another record closing high on Tuesday, but ended well off its intra-day record high as a strong rally fizzled during the afternoon on fears of a share placement, traders said.
The Hang Seng index closed 14.13 points higher at 13,056.93 after hitting an all-time intra-day high at 13,183.01.
Turnover was a strong HK$10.48 billion compared to HK$8.26 billion on Monday.
"There are just placement rumours around the market. If you get a bull market you generally get placements," said Rory McAllister at HSBC James Capel.

Traders said the market's record levels had prompted fears that one of the major blue-chip companies would carry out a share placement. They said potential candidates were Sun Hung Kai Properties, which closed down HK$1.00 at HK$92.25, and HSBC Holdings, which finished HK$2.00 lower at HK$158.00.
Sun Hung Kai Properties denied rumours that it would place shares. An HSBC spokesman said the company declined to comment on market speculation.
Analysts said although the market pared its gains in late-trading, investors remained bullish on the Hong Kong market and particularly the property sector.
Shares in Cheung Kong rose HK$1.50 to HK$68.50 and Henderson Land advanced HK$1.00 to HK$73.25. Brokers said both shares were boosted by talk of covered warrant issues.
"Despite all the warnings of consolidation, it looks like local funds and Chinese funds from mainland China are still buying," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International.

"The China factor is still favorable and in fact it is turning more positive -- inflation is down in China and China assures us that the financial system in Hong Kong will remain intact (beyond Hong Kong's reversion to China)," he said.
Tang said even at current levels, Hong Kong stocks were not considered expensive and compared to other regional markets, Hong Kong remained attractive.
He said technically the market was overbought but could go higher before pausing.
"A lot of people would like to see it take a breather but there is a lot of momentum," added McAllister.
Shares in Hang Seng Bank finished the session HK$1.50 lower at HK$93.50. Hutchison gained HK$1.00 to HK$61.50.
November Hang Seng futures rose 35 points to 13,055.
